key_insight: UR-VC shows that demo time is an imperfect proxy for task progress in robot learning, and that this noisy signal can be corrected without manual labels. By unsupervisedly refining progress/value estimates, the method makes dense supervision more reliable for downstream robotic learning.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the lack of accurate dense progress or value labels for robotic manipulation tasks. It tackles the problem of using normalized demonstration time as a noisy substitute for true physical progress, especially in contact-rich settings where time and task completion can diverge.
method: Uses normalized time within demonstrations as an initial progress proxy.
Applies unsupervised robotic value correction to adjust noisy time-derived labels toward more physically meaningful progress estimates.
Improves dense signals used for policy learning, intermediate-state evaluation, and task completion detection without requiring manual annotation.
impact: This matters because many robot learning pipelines depend on dense reward/value supervision that is expensive or unavailable at scale. UR-VC offers a practical way to improve these signals from demonstration data, which can lead to more robust learning and better task success in real-world robotic manipulation.

paper_title: UR-VC: Unsupervised Robotic Value Correction for Time-Derived Progress Proxies
paper_authors: Lirui Zhao, Modi Shi, Li Chen, Qi Liu, Ping Luo
